messages:
miranda: Hey team, customer "optic" on dedicated pool eu-west-2 reporting sudden 95th pct latency jump ~07:10 UTC, and a few 429s. Not huge error volume but consistent. Can we check noisy neighbor or autoscale behavior? :thinking:

raj: pinging infra — any recent autoscale events for eu-west-2-dedicated?

support-bot: Autoscale event: +2 nodes to eu-west-2-dedicated-pool at 07:12:03 UTC (trigger: CPU/SM avg > 82%).

devon: I pulled the call traces — requests are getting queued at our fronting router for ~80-120ms then token generation spikes to +400ms. Kernel slots show one tenant consuming sustained SM utilization.

miranda: put logs + sample request IDs: req_0a1f, req_0a2b, req_0a9c. Customer says it started after a scheduled model switch by their app.

raj: grabbing host mapping now. Can you confirm the node(s) these requests landed on?

devon: looks like most of those requests hit host eu-west-2-node-07, MIG profile 1g.12gb (3 slices).

eva: running quick NV check on node-07. nvidia-smi top says one container is at 98% SM, memory 85%. Others are idle.

devon: thats suspicious — might be a tenant launching a high-SM workload (beam search or repeated long contexts). Any cgroup isolation oddities?

miranda: I ran a short repro by replaying one request on a test replica and saw the same backend latency bump when co-located.

raj: sharing commands I ran: 
```
# list MIG slices and pci ids
sudo nvidia-smi mig -lgi
# per-process utilization
sudo docker exec -it container_id nvidia-smi dmon -s u
```

raj: output excerpt: 
```
GPU  MIG     SM   MEM
0    1g.12g  98%  84%
0    1g.5g   12%  10%
```

devon: also checked kernel logs, saw repeated scheduler preemption events + minor ECC logs but nothing fatal. dmesg shows no OOM.

miranda: Does our runtime respect per-slice SM caps? Shouldn't the MIG partition prevent one slice from saturating others?

raj: MIG isolates most resources but we do see SM scheduling variability when slices are misconfigured — e.g., if a tenant's workload spawns many CUDA contexts across multiple slices, it can cause cross-slice contention on shared L2/L3 and host-side PCIe bandwidth.

devon: I suspect the tenant's model switch moved them to a larger seq-length/prefill pattern, increasing PCIe transfers and host copy pressure. That explains router queue + token latency.

miranda: Any quick mitigations we can apply while we investigate the tenant behavior?

raj: short-term options: 1) move the noisy tenant off node-07 to a quieter host via live migrate; 2) bump autoscale further to reduce per-node load; 3) enforce per-tenant rate-limits to soften burst.

eva: I kicked migration for tenant optic -> eu-west-2-node-11 at 07:18 UTC. Also temporarily increased pool target by +1 at 07:19.

support-bot: Migration job optic -> eu-west-2-node-11 started (job-76823). Estimated 30s cutover.

devon: after migration, tail latency for the sampled requests dropped ~60-70ms and SM utilization on node-07 fell to ~45%. Not perfect but much better.

miranda: good — customer reports improvement. We should still root cause: whether tenant workload is misbehaving or our scheduling needs tuning.

raj: action items: (1) ask customer for their model config + sequence length distribution and recent app change notes (miranda) (2) collect perf counters from node-07 across the incident window: L2/L3 bandwidth, PCIe TX/RX, context switches (devon) (3) review cgroup/ML runtime flags for multi-context spawning (eva)

miranda: I'll loop in the account team and get the model config. Noting customer said they switched from greedy->beam search which would match the higher SM + PCIe churn.

devon: flagging potential infra improvement: add a scheduler heuristic to prefer tenant packing that minimizes high-PCIe neighbors on same host. Filing infra ticket if we see recurring pattern.

miranda: marking thread resolved for now since customer sees improvement. Will post updates once we get the model config and perf counters. :white_check_mark: 

raj: thanks everyone. I'll keep the migration and autoscale logs attached to the incident for postmortem.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1493 — "dedicated pool transient saturation due to tenant bursty beam search". Assigned to devon, eva.

miranda: closing loop — customer accepted mitigation and removed their beam flag temporarily. We'll re-open if it recurs.
